findings.issue: Ran 'pgrep -f entry.mjs | xargs -r kill' inside the invoking bash command ~10 times; the pattern matches the shell's own command line, killing it (exit 143) and forcing a retry turn each time, even after identifying the cause at turns 53 and 110.
findings.suggestion: Kill by PID (pgrep output captured, then kill) or use a pattern that can't self-match (e.g. pgrep -f 'dist/server/entry[.]mjs'), or use a single supervisor script for start/stop.

findings.issue: Attempted two edits against bugs it misremembered writing (index.astro syntax error, wrong import path); the files were already correct, so both edits failed and a verification turn was spent confirming nothing was wrong.
findings.suggestion: Grep/read the actual file before editing from memory.

findings.issue: Mobile moves-table fix looped four times because screenshots were stale from browser cache before the CSS change was confirmed absent from the rendered page; one full rebuild/restart cycle was wasted.
findings.suggestion: When a change appears to have no effect, first confirm the built asset content (it did this at turn 101, but only after a wasted cycle) and hard-reload the browser.

summary: A strong, well-sequenced session: the agent front-loaded spec/test/data/screenshot analysis, de-risked its assumptions before coding, and passed the full 54-test suite on the first run, then used screenshot diffing to catch and fix two real bugs the tests don't cover. Debugging of the harness-probe failure (IPv6-only bind) and the CSS-cache mystery was root-cause quality. The main blemish is process hygiene: it repeated a self-killing pkill command ten times across the session despite diagnosing it twice, wasting roughly a dozen turns on retries and hallucinated-bug edits.
